purpose: Cross-chat coordination and rollcall for Gef feature work. This file is a progress index only. It MUST point to canonical sources of truth and MUST NOT become a second authority for lesson readiness, language membership, lexical truth, corpus evidence, review state, or release state.

owns: Lexi annotation-pass catalog and graph mapping

rules: work_state, reconciliation_state, and coverage_state are tracker coordination fields only.
integrity review and release are separate axes and MUST NOT be collapsed into work_state.
Any copied authoritative review/release/readiness value MUST include source_ref and, when practical, source_pointer or source_id.
Language membership and total language counts MUST be derived from gef-expo/registry/language-support.json, never hardcoded here.
Lesson readiness MUST be resolved from curriculum/lesson-system-manifest.json using its canonical precedence. This tracker may cache a result only with its direction and source reference.
Lexical authority and lesson readiness are independent. Lexicon depth never promotes a lesson release state.
Tier 3 Core coverage never implies Full grammar support.
Unknown or missing evidence stays unknown/missing. Do not fill progress cells optimistically.

feature_map.notes: Tracker does not summarize lesson readiness into one status. Read the canonical manifest for actual part/language-direction readiness.
Lexi is subordinate to the lesson SSOT for lesson eligibility/readiness and to Expo for product language membership.
No language list is duplicated in this tracker. Per-language rollcall rows use language_tag keys resolved against the Expo registry.
Review state, release state, trust, and tracker work progress remain separate dimensions.

rules: Use source_language_tag + target_language_tag for directional lesson readiness or pair-specific work.
Use language_tag for non-directional lexicon/Lexi/runtime coverage.
Do not add all 104 language rows merely to say unknown. Add rows when a chat has concrete status/evidence to report.
Every evidence_refs entry must point to the owning repo/file, issue, PR, validator, or canonical object that justifies the status.

instructions: Every chat working on Gef should read this file before its final handoff when practical.
Add or update one rollcall entry for the work actually inspected or changed.
Name exact repos/files/PRs touched. Do not claim completion outside the scope actually verified.
If another chat changed an authority file since your check, set reconciliation_state to not_checked or needs_update rather than assuming alignment.
Prefer stable workstream_id values so later chats update the same lane instead of creating duplicates.

completed: Lexi uses the lesson schema typed-ref vocabulary instead of inventing parallel target types.
Lexi keeps lesson readiness/review/release external and independent from lexical authority.
Lexi modular integrations point to canonical owners rather than copying their truth.
Tier 3 is Core-only for lesson discovery/read/game behavior and cannot become Full grammar from lexicon depth.
Corpus occurrence annotations remain content-owned and cannot authorize lesson exposure by themselves.
Central FEATURE_PROGRESS.json tracker added without editing the canonical lesson or Lexi manifests.
remaining_or_external: Future lesson/Lexi edits should re-run reconciliation and update this rollcall entry if canonical contracts change.
Per-language rows should be populated only as concrete language/feature work is verified.
Open PR/CI/deployment state must be rechecked by the central tracker because those states can change independently.
